relevance_note: The paper describes 16 HA20 patients individually in Table 2 ('Sixteen patients from 6 families of European ancestry with HA20 were studied'), HA20 being 'driven by pathogenic variants in TNFAIP3', but it prints no variant for any patient.
method_note: Read the full Markdown. The only patient-level data are in Table 2 (16 rows, patients as rows). A short Python script transcribed Table 2 cells; I checked the parse cell by cell against my own independent typing of all 16 rows (exact match, asserted in the script). Labels: Table 2 numbers patients in a column headed 'Patient number' and families in a column headed 'Family'; I recorded them as 'Patient N' and 'Family N'. Table 2 cells are coded 1/0 with no legend; I read 1 = present and 0 = absent because the column totals match the text (mouth ulcers 16/16 'Mouth ulcers were described in 16 patients (100%)'; genital ulcers 13/16; gut symptoms 13/16 = 'Abdominal symptoms ... in 13 patients (81%)'), so 0 was recorded as excluded (stated for this individual). Checklist: a 0 for 'History of colitis/gut ulcers' was left 'not reported' for 'gastrointestinal ulcers or inflammation' because it is narrower than that item (e.g. gastritis is not covered). No TNFAIP3 variant (cDNA, protein or genomic) is printed for any patient; 'mutational status' was extracted from records but not reported, so the variants table is empty. Sex and age are given only as cohort aggregates (Table 1), so they are 'not reported' per person. Ethnicity 'European ancestry' is taken from a statement covering all 16 patients. Not attributable to numbered patients and therefore not recorded: liver MRI findings (5 unnamed patients), liver/stomach/ileal/colon histology, interferon signature (5/5 unnamed), elevated liver enzymes (4 unnamed), Table 1 colitis 4 and GI ulcer 7, and the Discussion statement 'no patient displayed auto-antibodies specific to PSC' (unclear whether all 16 were tested; also narrower than the autoantibody checklist item). The paper does not say which three of the six families were previously described (refs 11-13). Contradictions/oddities: Table 1 'Females | 12 (71)' (12/16 is 75%) and controls '25 (78)' with n = 22; Table 1 'Abdominal pain' on collection day 4 (25) vs Table 2 'GI symptoms on collection day' = 1 for only 3 patients (1, 9, 11); Table 2 'Liver disease' = 1 for 5 patients vs 'Elevated liver enzymes' in 4 (different concepts, not treated as a contradiction); spleen lengths printed as '163 and 160 cm'.
